clue.text: Those who lash out at one taking a little snooze are like one referred to as a little monster.

definitions.text: one referred to as a little monster

parts.note: people who lash out at someone whip them, so they are whippers
someone taking a nap is a napper

explanation.surface: People who strike at a dozing child are compared to the brat they call a little monster.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippersnapper is a cheeky, presumptuous young person, the sort an exasperated adult might call a little monster.

clue.text: See 30 across
They did a lot of fighting during the Civil War, as a way to press a number of little boys with it.

definitions.text: They did a lot of fighting during the Civil War

parts.note: one irons clothes to press them
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
lads are boys

explanation.surface: A history of the Civil War drifts into pressing clothes with a crowd of children.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironclads were armoured warships, such as the Monitor and the Merrimack, that fought in the American Civil War.

clue.text: Where Mr. Ed could be kept in one's living quarters (as some say) to cut off the tail.

definitions.text: Where Mr. Ed could be kept

parts.note: pad is slang for one's flat or home
to dock an animal is to cut its tail short

explanation.surface: Wondering where to keep the TV talking horse at home, and whether to bob its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Mister Ed was a talking horse in a 1960s American sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddock is a small enclosed field where horses are kept, fitting a famous horse.

clue.text: The so-called daily grind might be a way to tell on a running contest.

parts.note: to rat on someone is to inform on them
a race is a contest of speed

explanation.surface: Everyday drudgery might be one way to inform on a sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is an idiom for the competitive, exhausting routine of working life.

clue.text: See 1
The wrong name on a single flower.

indicators.note: placed on, so the next part follows in the answer
a wrong name is a muddled one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word name, taken as written, supplies the letters to be mixed
a single thing is one

explanation.surface: A mislabelled flower card bearing an incorrect name.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone, or windflower, is a plant with bright cup-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Rather nicey-nicey, to a point–as one might describe a number.

definitions.text: as one might describe a number

parts.note: prim means prudishly proper
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A sugary, overpolite manner is described, with a nod to numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a point' looks like a hedge meaning somewhat; here it adds a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime describes a whole number divisible only by itself and one, such as seven or eleven.

clue.text: Used to control the current flow, but her toast is no good this way.

definitions.text: Used to control the current flow

indicators.note: her toast as written is no good, so its letters must be rearranged

parts.note: the words her toast, taken as written, supply the letters

explanation.surface: An electrician dismisses a wedding speech as useless for controlling the current.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheostat is a variable resistor that adjusts the strength of an electric current.

clue.text: Broken plates could still hold a major element of food.

indicators.note: broken plates are in pieces, so the letters are put back together differently

parts.note: the word plates, taken as written, supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Even cracked crockery can still carry a main dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a basic, principal food such as rice or bread that forms much of a diet.

clue.text: Considered sufficient by some people.

parts.note: points to the proverb that such a thing is sufficient
the people meant are the wise, who need only a hint

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'A word to the wise is sufficient': the clue gives the proverb's verdict and leaves the solver to name the thing judged sufficient.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying holds that a brief hint is enough for a sensible person, so this phrase is what the proverb calls sufficient.

clue.text: See 10
Indian chief with nothing sort of close on a combination of it.

indicators.note: placed on, so the next piece follows in the answer

parts.note: nothing is zero, written as the letter O

indicators.note: a sort of close is a loose version of it, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word close, taken as written, supplies the letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a Native American leader closing in on some combination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combination of it' merely tells the solver the answer is assembled from these parts. OSCEOLA was a Seminole leader in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: Osceola led the Seminole people in resisting removal from Florida in the 1830s, a famous Native American chief.

clue.text: Is a sea god capable of assuming different shapes in favor of fatback?

definitions.text: a sea god capable of assuming different shapes

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
fat is SUET, and back says to read it backwards

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether a shape-shifting sea deity supports pork fat.
explanation.walkthrough: Fatback looks like the cut of pork; it splits into fat (suet) read back.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Proteus is the old man of the sea who changes form to avoid capture, hence the word protean.

clue.text: One doesn't have to be a football player to approach a job this way.

definitions.text: One doesn't have to be a football player to approach a job this way.

parts.note: a lineman's position in American football, whose job is bringing down the ball carrier
the same word as a verb means setting about a task with determination

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is both a gridiron position and a verb for setting about work, so anyone can do it without wearing pads.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a job energetically is to tackle it, and a tackle is also an offensive or defensive lineman.

clue.text: Vote in an old god–one whom mourning becomes, even in play.

definitions.text: one whom mourning becomes, even in play

parts.note: to vote someone in is to elect them
Ra was the sun god of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: Electing an ancient deity sounds like the plot of a theatrical tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene O'Neill's play is titled Mourning Becomes Electra.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of O'Neill's trilogy names this figure as the one mourning becomes, a literary allusion.

clue.text: John the naturalist rises to that which one hopes is firma–and loaded with specimens.

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, a container that is loaded with specimens

parts.words: that which one hopes is firma
parts.note: terra firma is solid ground, so terra is the word paired with firma

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the name is read upwards

parts.note: John Muir was the naturalist who founded the Sierra Club

explanation.surface: A naturalist climbs toward solid ground with a box full of samples.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrarium is a glass case for keeping plants or small animals, a container full of living specimens.

clue.text: See 30 across
One held for ransom is sort of a ghost, to a point.

indicators.note: added to, so the point follows the rearranged letters
a sort of ghost is a garbled version, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the word ghost, taken as written, joins the a in the mix
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A kidnap victim is compared to a phantom, up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a point' reads as a hedge meaning partly; here it adds a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a captive kept until a ransom or demand is met.

clue.text: Made sure the figures were right by sitting in on the class?

definitions.text: Made sure the figures were right
definitions.meaning: first meaning: inspected the accounts officially
second meaning: attended a course without taking it for credit

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses belong to one verb: an accountant checks the books, and a student sits in on a course without credit.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor examines financial records, and in American colleges one may audit a course by attending without credit.

clue.text: Geometrician who brought up a hint on a hat, as some say.

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a cue is a prompting hint
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A mathematician who mentioned a clue about headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid of Alexandria wrote the Elements, the founding textbook of geometry.

clue.text: They supposedly fly, but one shouldn't believe many of them.

definitions.text: They supposedly fly, but one shouldn't believe many of them.

parts.note: gossip is said to fly around, as in the idiom about stories flying

parts.words: one shouldn't believe many of them
parts.note: stories passed on by word of mouth are often false

explanation.walkthrough: Flying suggests birds or saucers; the idiom is that gossip flies.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories passed around by word of mouth, with no proof, are said to fly and are often untrue.

clue.text: Emblems of royalty concerning the common young lady with a first-class upbringing.

parts.note: re means about, as in a letter heading
gal is the informal word for a girl

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing up means the piece is read upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the digit written as the letter I

explanation.surface: An ordinary girl with an excellent upbringing earns the trappings of royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the crown jewels and other symbols of a monarch's office.

clue.text: Behold! It's inside the practitioner–and has quite a tuneful combination.

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective for music that has a tuneful combination of notes

indicators.note: the exclamation goes inside the word for a doctor

parts.note: a medic is a medical practitioner
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Look! Inside the doctor is something rather musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodic describes music with a pleasing tune, a combination of notes that sounds sweet.

clue.text: He rowed people across the Styx–giving a drink (as the Brits say) to Mr. Reagan.

definitions.text: He rowed people across the Styx

parts.note: cha, or char, is British slang for tea
Ronald Reagan, shortened to Ron

explanation.surface: The mythical boatman offers a cup of tea to an American president.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Charon is the ferryman who carries the souls of the dead across the river Styx.

clue.text: Kinda angry when a false coin is about to be known as the kind that just floats around!

definitions.text: the kind that just floats around

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the angry word
a false version of the word coin has its letters jumbled

parts.note: the word coin, taken as written, supplies the letters
mad is a casual word for angry

explanation.surface: Someone gets irritated by a counterfeit coin that keeps drifting from hand to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic peoples wander rather than settle, so the word describes those who drift about with no fixed home.

clue.text: Remember this boat? It's in quite a state!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the battleship in 'Remember the ...', the rallying cry of 1898
second meaning: the New England state

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite a state' reads as quite a mess; it is literally a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: The USS Maine exploded in Havana harbour in 1898, and it shares its name with the northeasternmost US state.

clue.text: A big one, but something slung lowered him down.

definitions.text: A big one, but something slung lowered him down.

parts.note: points to a giant
David felled the giant with a stone from his sling

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowered him down' sounds like a rope; the slung thing is David's slingshot stone.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the Philistine giant is killed by young David's sling, so a slung stone brought the big man down.

clue.text: Responsible for much ground, but bad grits made a large number sick.

indicators.note: bad grits are spoilt, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word grits, taken as written, supplies the letters
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Spoiled grits from a farm grinding much grain made many people ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Ground is the past participle of grind, not soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A gristmill grinds grain into flour, so it is responsible for producing a lot of ground meal.

clue.text: Sort of rid the queen of what is less damp.

indicators.note: a sort of rid is a reshuffled one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word rid, taken as written, supplies the letters
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A puzzling request to rid the monarch of something less soggy.
explanation.definitionFit: Drier is the comparative of dry, meaning having less moisture.

clue.text: Puts one's foot down, getting to take in the paper in the back street.

indicators.note: the reading goes inside the reversed abbreviation
the street abbreviation is read back to front

parts.note: to take in a newspaper is to read it

explanation.surface: Someone takes a firm stand while reading a newspaper in an alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts one's foot down' sounds like insisting; here it is literal walking.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread is literally to set one's foot down when walking.

clue.text: A question posed the checker-up, after dark.

definitions.text: A question posed the checker-up, after dark.

parts.note: the one who checks up is a guard, asked for a report
the question concerns the hours of darkness

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Isaiah 21:11, where a sentry is asked for news of the night; 'checker-up' is a whimsical name for the sentry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible verse is literally a question put to a sentry about the night, the dark hours he guards.
